tool.name: get_conversion_insights
tool.title: Get Conversion Insights
tool.description: Return the confused-vs-calm conversion analysis: it splits the site's sessions into a "confused" cohort (produced at least one friction signal) and a "calm" cohort (zero friction), then compares conversion rate, session duration, pages per session, and bounce rate between them. Use it to state plainly how much less confused sessions convert (e.g. "confused sessions convert 12 points lower"), which pages and traffic sources bleed the most conversions to confusion, and the ranked insights. cohorts/deltas are the headline; by_page and by_source break the gap down; insights[] are pre-written narratable findings (check `confident` before quoting a number, and note low_confidence cohorts). What counts as a conversion comes from the site's configured conversion goal. Optional days (1-90, default 7).

tool.name: query_raw_rows
tool.title: Query Raw Rows
tool.description: Return SQL-style raw rows from an allowlisted Flusterduck table, scoped to the authorized site. Default 100 rows sorted by the table's time column, newest first. Filters only apply where they make sense: event_type on events, signal_type on signals, status on ux_issues/alerts, session_id on events/signals/sessions.

limit.description: Max rows to return. Default 100, max 1000.

since.description: Only rows at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp, e.g. "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z".

table.description: Which table to read: events, signals, sessions, page_scores, score_history, ux_issues, alerts, or deploys.

until.description: Only rows at or before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

status.description: ux_issues or alerts tables only: filter by status. Issues: open, triaged, in_progress, verified, resolved, ignored, regressed. Alerts: fired, acknowledged, investigating, resolved.

site_id.description: Site UUID. Optional when this connection is scoped to one site (the default for site-scoped keys); required when the connection is org-wide. whoami shows the scope.

sort_by.description: Sort column; must be allowlisted for the table (the API answers 400 listing valid columns if not). Defaults to the table's time column, e.g. occurred_at for events and signals.

sort_dir.description: Sort direction: asc or desc. Default desc.

event_type.description: events table only: filter by event type, e.g. "click", "pageview", "error".

tool.name: explore
tool.title: Explore
tool.description: Run a deterministic, typed query against a site's session data. No natural language, no LLM: a closed vocabulary the engine validates before touching a row, built explicitly so an agent can compose it directly. Give it a window (window_days, 1-90, default 7) and up to 12 AND-ed filters over a fixed field list: signal (a friction/heuristic type, e.g. "rage_click", "dead_click", "form_abandonment"), page (exact path, or substring with op "contains"), source (referrer/utm source, exact or "contains"), confused (boolean: session produced at least one friction signal), converted (boolean: session reached the site's configured conversion event), event_type (one of click, move, scroll, keyboard, form_focus, form_blur, form_submit, touch, navigation, error, signal, pageview, custom_signal, performance, visibility, sdk_error). Ops are is / is_not / contains. contains only makes sense for page and source; signal and the boolean fields only take is/is_not (contains is coerced to is for signal). Then choose exactly one output. {mode: "list", limit?, offset?} returns matching sessions (id, timing, pages visited, signal counts, source, confused/converted) ranked most-recent-first, limit 1-200 (default 50) with offset for paging: use it to pull concrete example sessions as evidence. Or {mode: "measure", metric, group_by?} computes metric ("count" | "avg_pageviews" | "conversion_rate" | "avg_dwell_ms" | "bounce_rate") as a single scalar, or as a series when group_by is set ("page" | "source" | "day" | "signal" | "cohort", where "cohort" splits confused vs. calm sessions). Example: "sessions that rage-clicked on /pricing in the last 7 days" -> filters: [{field:"page",op:"is",value:"/pricing"},{field:"signal",op:"is",value:"rage_click"}], output: {mode:"list"}. Example: "does confusion actually hurt conversion here?" -> output: {mode:"measure",metric:"conversion_rate",group_by:"cohort"}.

output.description: Exactly one output mode: {mode:"list"} for example sessions or {mode:"measure"} for a metric.

filters.description: Up to 12 AND-ed filters. Omit to match every session in the window.

Trigger types: spike (sudden confusion jump), anomaly (statistical deviation from baseline), new_page (a new page starts generating friction), trend (sustained drift), co_occurrence (many users confused at the same time), positive (score drops BELOW the threshold; fires on improvement), budget (confusion budget burn), revenue_threshold (estimated revenue at risk), stalled_signups (signup flow stalls). _published_faq.name: How do I add flusterduck to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add flusterduck to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.flusterduck.com/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is flusterduck MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, flusterduck scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is flusterduck's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, flusterduck scores 80/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 30 of 30 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to flusterduck?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to flusterduck in data-analytics on the Manufact MCP catalog include Epicure, Newsflash, Point Topic, Pricing Optimizer AI, and StatCite.

_published_faq.name: How can flusterduck improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: explore is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 55/100. No output schema is declared. Add one for structured results so clients can interpret returned fields.
